one_line: A 35-second 2D cartoon under a fixed 'PoV - 2 days without Mom' label in which a mother in a red sari walks in on a wrecked house (smashed vase, spilled water, burnt pot, dad knocked out on the floor) and ends with an exasperated face while the family clings to her legs.

hook.visual: Locked shot of a closed brown door on a pale pink wall and grey tiles, with the title label across the top; a shot of the wrecked living room follows at 1.5 s.
hook.on_screen_text: PoV - 2 days without Mom + a smiling-face emoji (white label with black text, same position in every frame from 0.0 to 34.5 s)
hook.why_it_stops_the_scroll: The label states a universal premise in 5 words from frame 0, the closed door raises 'what is behind it?', and the first gag arrives by 1.5 s (dad slumped on the floor, boy limp on the sofa). The saturated red sari is the only strong colour on a pastel set, so Mom pulls the eye when she appears at 3.0 s (observed + inferred).

beats.observed: Closed brown door, pale pink wall, grey tile floor. Title label at the top.
beats.spoken: Whisper marks only '(upbeat music)' at 0.0 to 2.6 s; no speech.
beats.on_screen_text: PoV - 2 days without Mom + smiling-face emoji

beats.observed: Living room aftermath: a dad in a vest and checked lungi sits on the floor with his head back, a boy in a blue top lies limp on a yellow sofa, a spiky dark rug on the tiles.
Mother in a red sari and green blouse, with a shoulder bag and a bindi, stands in the doorway with a small smile. At 4.5 a girl with cat-ear hairband and pink skirt stands crying with her arms out.

Messy bedroom: cardboard boxes, a cricket bat, a ball, clothes and scattered small objects on the floor. The girl holds an adult's hand (red sari at the edge) at 7.5; at 9.0 Mom gasps with both hands at her cheeks.

Mom walks through, frame blurred at 10.5, with the boy at the right edge drawn upside down with a mirrored shape below him (looks like a transition glitch). At 12.0 the frame is darkened; Mom and the boy look at a smashed flower pot and spilled water, and at 13.5 a close-up of the shards.

Kitchen sink piled with dirty pots with green stink fumes; the girl grimaces (15.0), Mom shouts with her mouth wide open (16.5). At 18.0 the boy skids on a puddle from a tipped green bucket with motion lines, and at 19.5 a faded copy of the boy lies in the puddle while the same boy also stands next to Mom, who covers her mouth.

Dad in a vest with a moustache lifts the lid off a pot and steam bursts out (22.5), his face goes from panic to dejection (24.0 to 25.5), the pot is black and burnt on the stove (27.0), then he lies flat on his back on the tiles with stars circling his head (28.5 to 30.0).
beats.spoken: Whisper marks '(singing in foreign language)' from 30.0 s to 34.1 s.

beats.observed: Dad (crying) and both kids hug Mom's legs. Mom presses her fingers to her forehead with her eyes shut, then half-opens them in tired irritation. The video ends on this face.

payoff: Two payoffs: the dad-knocked-out gag at 28.5 to 30.0 s, and the final emotional beat at 31.5 to 34.5 s where the family grovels at Mom's legs and she holds her forehead in exasperation. The caption promises 'Watch till the end to see how everyone struggles without Mom'.
cta: Caption only: 'Watch till the end', and 'like, comment, and share if you love your Mom'. Nothing on screen except the fixed PoV label.
share_or_comment_trigger: Mom-appreciation framing invites 'tag your mom' sends, and every household recognises the 'nothing works without her' joke. The caption asks directly to share if you love your Mom (stated in caption).
why_it_worked: 55,852,419 views vs an account median of 263,000 (212.4x): an already large channel had a top hit, so the format is strong beyond the channel's own base.

1.32% like rate (735,935 likes) is the highest of this batch and well above the 0.3% paid flag; the universal 'mom does everything' premise is on screen from frame 0 and no language is needed because the story is carried by drawn faces and gags (observed + inferred).

A new gag or room every 1.5 to 3 seconds for 35 seconds (messy room, vase, dishes, puddle, pot, knockout) plus a pay-off reaction at the end keeps people watching to the final face; only 2,300 comments (about 0.004%) means it spread by sharing rather than discussion (inferred).
paid_signal: no: like rate 1.32% is well above 0.3%, and the channel median of 263,000 shows an established audience, so 212x is read as an organic hit (inferred).

solo_route.how: 1) Write a 14 to 16 shot list of 1.5 to 2.5 seconds each: a closed door, the wrecked room, the parent arrives, then four escalating messes, ending on the parent's exasperated face. 2) Generate each shot as a vertical still in LumeBook's own illustration style, with the LumeBook child hero as the recurring chaos kid and simple fixed designs for the parent(s); reuse the same reference image so outfits and faces stay the same. 3) Animate with simple moves in CapCut (slow zoom, shake on impact, quick blur transitions) or image-to-video for 2 to 3 seconds per shot; hold longer on reaction faces. Skip voices: the original has music only per Whisper, so use a licensed sound from the platform's own library. 4) Put one fixed label at the top for the whole video in the same position, e.g. 'POV: יומיים בלי אמא', and finish on a 2-second LumeBook end card. About 3 to 5 hours for the first one, much less for later episodes once the characters exist.
solo_route.needs: Nothing, but avoid copying this video's characters and avoid the 'useless dad' trope if dads are part of the gifter audience.

lumebook_version.concept: Same escalating-mess 2D skit with LumeBook's illustrated child hero as the chaos kid and a parent as the reactor; the last shot cuts to the hero on the printed book cover on a shelf, calm and still, as 'the only version of him that listens', with a free-preview prompt.

evidence_notes: OBSERVED: 24 frames at 1.5 s intervals. Flat-colour digital cartoon style with black outlines; a single title label is in the same spot in every frame. AI or not: I cannot tell. Line weight and shading differ from shot to shot, which fits both hand-drawn digital illustration and AI-generated stills. Artifacts that could point to AI image-to-video or to a rough transition: at 10.5 s the boy at the right edge is upside down with a mirrored shape beneath him and the frame is blurred; at 12.0 and 21.0 s frames are darkened; at 18.0 and 19.5 s the same boy appears twice in one frame (standing next to Mom and lying in the puddle, the latter semi-transparent at 19.5 s), which looks like overlaid animation layers or a generation artifact. Character designs (red sari with green blouse and bindi, cat-ear hairband on the girl, blue-shirt boy, moustached dad in a vest) stay consistent across shots. The meta field ai_made_how says illustrated_comic and no tool is named in the caption or frames. The dad on the floor at 1.5 s and again at 28.5 s suggests the opening is a flash-forward or a repeated beat (inferred). SPOKEN: Whisper returned only '(upbeat music)' at 0.0 to 2.6 s and '(singing in foreign language)' at 30.0 to 34.1 s, so there is no usable speech transcript and the video appears to have no dialogue (inferred); I cannot hear the music. I read the caption ('Mom not at home', 'burnt food', 'desi family comedy') as the account's own framing; made_by is the channel's own account. The reading that Mom is returning home after two days is inferred from the door shot, her bag and the order of reveals. LIKENESS AND CONSENT: all characters are cartoons, no real child, no celebrity look-alike, no real voices. Other flags: the soundtrack may be licensed or copyrighted music, so LumeBook should use the platform's own commercial library; the family is drawn with South Asian cultural markers and a 'helpless dad' gender trope, which should not be copied into an Israeli brand context without thought.
